name: Beyond the Edge of the Map: Silk Road to Everest
description: Merchants, admirals, sailors and mountaineers who crossed oceans, found new lands and reached the poles and the highest summit.

checkpoints.name: Early journeys
checkpoints.note: Zhang Qian's mission west from China around 138 BCE opened routes later called the Silk Road, the monk Xuanzang walked to India and back in the 600s, and Leif Erikson's Norse crew reached North America around the year 1000, as the site at L'Anse aux Meadows shows.

checkpoints.name: Travellers by land and sea
checkpoints.note: Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta and Zheng He travel to the farthest courts and ports of the known world, and Prince Henry sends Portuguese ships down the African coast.

checkpoints.name: The ocean opens
checkpoints.note: Dias rounds Africa, Columbus crosses the Atlantic, Da Gama reaches India and Magellan's fleet, finished by Elcano, sails around the world.

checkpoints.name: New worlds charted
checkpoints.note: French, English and Dutch navigators such as Cartier, Drake, Hudson, Champlain, Tasman and Cook map coasts and rivers on every continent.

checkpoints.name: Interiors and poles
checkpoints.note: Humboldt, Lewis and Clark and Livingstone cross continents, while Amundsen, Scott and Shackleton race across the ice of Antarctica.

checkpoints.name: The last summit
checkpoints.note: In 1924 Mallory and Irvine vanished near the summit of Everest, and in 1953 Hillary and Tenzing stood on top, one of the last great feats of exploration on Earth.
